title: New Car vs Used Car at 20: The $16,000 Difference
summary: Leo and Nia are both 20, with the same job and the same pay. Their car payments are only about $140 a month apart, yet after seven years Leo has spent about $16,000 more once you subtract what each car is still worth. This video covers seven things to understand about the real cost of your first car: the out-the-door price, 84-month loans, depreciation and being underwater, insurance for young drivers, the all-in monthly cost, buying used carefully, and keeping a car after it's paid off, plus honesty checks on used-car risks and the 20/4/10 rule. Examples assume a $32,000 new car and a $16,000 four-year-old used car, 8% taxes and fees, Q3 2026 average loan rates (7.0% new, 10.6% used), depreciation of 20% then 15% a year (new) and 10% a year (used), Bankrate's 2026 average full-coverage premium for a 19-year-old, and $220 or $280 a month for gas and upkeep; they are illustrations, not predictions. Leo and Nia are fictional composites.
